hero.title: ZenStats Documentation
hero.description: ZenStats is a self-hosted, privacy-first web analytics platform. Collect visitor data without third-party involvement, query it through a clean REST API, and stay fully in control of your infrastructure.

baseUrl.heading: Base URL
baseUrl.description: All API requests are made relative to your ZenStats instance URL.

responseFormat.heading: Response format
responseFormat.description: All endpoints return a consistent JSON envelope.

authentication.description: ZenStats supports two authentication methods. Choose based on your use case.

apiKey.heading: API Key
apiKey.description: Create an API key from your account settings. Pass it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
apiKey.callout: API keys grant read access to your analytics data. Store them securely and rotate them periodically from Settings → API Keys.

jwt.heading: JWT (dashboard sessions)
jwt.description: The web dashboard authenticates via short-lived JWT tokens issued at login. The token is refreshed automatically using a refresh token. This method is used internally by the dashboard and is not required for API integrations.

trackingScript.description: Add a single <script> tag to every page you want to track. No cookies are set by default.
trackingScript.note: Replace example.com with the domain you registered in ZenStats. Optional features (Tagged Events, Outbound Links, File Downloads, ...) are toggled on the site's Install page, which generates the matching script variant.

instrumentation.heading: Instrumentation overview
instrumentation.description: Every data point in ZenStats is an event: an event name (the n field) plus optional key/value properties. Pageviews are just events named pageview. There are four ways to record events:

ways.auto: Automatic — the script records pageviews, engagement and (if enabled) outbound clicks, downloads and form submissions with no extra code.
ways.tagged: Tagged elements — add a CSS class like event-name=Signup to any element; no JavaScript required.
ways.js: JavaScript API — call zenstats('Event Name', { props }) from your own code.
ways.server: Server-side — POST the event payload to /api/event from your backend (required for revenue today).

auto.heading: Built-in event names
auto.description: These names are reserved and emitted by the script itself. They show up in the event:name dimension like any custom event.

events.pageview: Always on. Sent on initial load, back/forward navigation and SPA route changes. Drives visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce_rate, and pageview goals.
events.engagement: Always on. Sent when the tab is hidden or the visitor leaves; carries active time and max scroll depth. Drives time_on_page and scroll_depth. Not counted in the events metric.
events.outbound: Requires the Outbound Links feature. Click on an <a> pointing to another domain; url property holds the target (without query string / fragment).
events.download: Requires the File Downloads feature. Click on a link ending with a tracked extension (data-file-types, default pdf, xlsx, docx, ...); url property holds the file.
events.form: Requires Tagged Events, Outbound Links or File Downloads. Any <form> submit without an event-name class.

auto.callout: Outbound Links, File Downloads and Tagged Events are compiled into the script variant you copy from the Install page — there is no HTML attribute to turn them on per element.

eventName.heading: Event names
eventName.description: The event name is the key that everything else hangs on: it is what you filter and break down by (event:name), what an event goal matches, and what funnel steps are built from.

rules.exact: Matching is exact and case-sensitive: Signup, signup and Sign Up are three different events. An event goal fires only when event_name equals the goal's name exactly.
rules.reserved: pageview and engagement are reserved for the script. Don't reuse them for custom events.
rules.stable: Pick a convention and keep names stable, e.g. Object: Action (Pricing: Click, Checkout: Complete). Renaming an event later splits its history.
rules.props: Keep variable data out of the name. Use properties instead: one Purchase event with plan=pro beats Purchase Pro / Purchase Team as separate names.

js.heading: Method 1 — JavaScript API
js.description: The script exposes a global zenstats(eventName, options) function. Options: props (object), interactive (boolean, default true), callback (function), and u / url for a manual pageview URL.

tagged.heading: Method 2 — Tagged elements (no code)
tagged.description: With the Tagged Events feature enabled, any element whose class list contains event-name=<Name> sends that event on click (or on submit for forms). Extra classes of the form event-<key>=<value> become properties.

rules.plus: Use + for spaces: event-name=Button+Click is recorded as "Button Click".
rules.parents: The clicked element and up to 3 parent levels are inspected, so tagging a wrapper works.
rules.link: For links the url property is filled automatically from href; tagged links are not double-counted as outbound clicks or downloads.

tagged.callout: Tagged Events must be enabled on the Install page (it changes the script file you embed). Without it the event-name classes are ignored.

props.heading: Custom properties
props.description: Properties are free-form key/value pairs attached to an event (props in the JS API, event-<key>=<value> classes, or the p object in the payload). Values are stored as strings. Query them with the event:props:<key> dimension or filter on them, e.g. ["is", "event:props:plan", ["pro"]].
props.callout: An event goal can also require properties (custom props). The goal then counts only events whose name matches and whose every listed property equals the given value.

server.heading: Method 3 — Server-side events
server.description: Anything you can't observe in the browser (payments, sign-up confirmations, API usage) can be posted straight to /api/event. n (event name), d (a registered and verified domain) and u (page URL) should always be set; p (properties), revenue and t (client timestamp, ISO 8601 within the last hour) are optional. Requests without Origin/Referer headers are accepted as server clients; if you do send them, the host must be the site domain or one of its configured allowed origins, otherwise the event is rejected with 403.

revenue.heading: Revenue (ecommerce)
revenue.description: Attach revenue to an event by including a revenue object; amount accepts a string or number, currency is an ISO code. Query it with the total_revenue / average_revenue metrics.
revenue.callout: The tracking script does not send revenue automatically yet — post the event (with the revenue field) to /api/event from your server or checkout flow, as in Method 3.

aggregate.description: Returns aggregated metrics for a site over a given time period. Optionally compare against a previous period.

breakdown.description: Returns a ranked breakdown of a dimension. Use this to build top-pages, top-sources, and country tables.

timeseries.description: Returns time-series data points for the main graph. Granularity is automatically chosen based on the period (hourly for day, daily for longer ranges).

currentVisitors.description: Returns the count of visitors active on the site within the last 5 minutes. Useful for a live indicator.

v2Query.description: A more flexible query API that accepts a JSON body. Supports multi-dimensional grouping, ordering, and offset-based pagination.

multiDim.heading: Multi-dimension breakdown
multiDim.description: Pass more than one dimension to cross-tabulate. Every result row includes a column for each dimension plus the metrics.

metrics.description: Metrics can be combined freely in most API calls. Some metrics (time_on_page, scroll_depth) require engagement tracking to be active.

dimensions.description: Dimensions define what to group by in breakdown and v2 queries. Use the prefixed form (visit:source) in API calls.

filters.description: Filters narrow results to a subset of traffic. Pass them as a JSON array, URL-encoded in GET requests or as a JSON field in POST requests.
filters.caseCallout: Filters are case-sensitive by default. Add a 4th tuple element {"case_sensitive": false} for case-insensitive matching.

periods.description: Pass the period key as the period query parameter. For custom ranges, use the date_range field in the v2 API.

goals.description: Goals measure how many visitors complete a specific action — a pageview or a custom event. Configure them in Site Settings → Goals.
goals.callout: Goal conversions appear in the Stats dashboard under the Goals tab once configured.

create.heading: Creating a goal
create.description: In Site Settings → Goals, click Add Goal. Choose between a Pageview goal (triggered when a visitor views a URL matching a pattern) or an Event goal (triggered when your tracking script fires a named event).

types.heading: Goal types
types.pageviewDesc: Triggered when a visitor views a URL that matches a pattern. Supports wildcards, e.g. /blog/*.
types.eventDesc: Triggered by a custom event — zenstats("EventName") in JS, an event-name=EventName class, or a server-side POST. The event name must match exactly (case-sensitive); optional custom props must all match too.

breakdown.heading: Querying goals
breakdown.description: Break down by the event:goal dimension to get one row per goal with its converters and conversion rate. conversion_rate is only available with a goal breakdown or a goal filter.
breakdown.callout: conversion_rate = unique converters of the goal ÷ total unique visitors in the period × 100.

funnels.description: Funnels show step-by-step conversion through a sequence of pages or events. Each step must be a defined goal.
funnels.callout: Funnel data is computed in real time — there is no pre-aggregation. For very high-traffic sites, limit the date range to keep query times low.

create.heading: Creating a funnel
create.description: In Site Settings → Funnels, add a funnel and select at least two goals as steps. Steps are evaluated in order — a visitor must complete step N before being counted in step N+1.

segments.description: Segments are reusable filter sets. Save a combination of filters as a named segment and apply it across the dashboard without re-entering the same filters.

management.heading: Segment API
management.list: List all segments for the site.

sharedLinks.description: Shared links let you share a read-only view of your stats with people who do not have a ZenStats account. The link contains a unique slug; anyone with the URL can view the stats.
sharedLinks.callout: Shared link views pass the slug as a ?slug= query parameter to all API calls. No authentication token is required.

create.heading: Creating a shared link
create.description: In Site Settings → Shared Links, click Create Link, give it a name, and copy the generated URL.

health.description: Use these endpoints in your container orchestration health checks. /live returns 200 when the process is running; /ready returns 200 when all backing services (ClickHouse, PostgreSQL) are reachable.

deployment.description: ZenStats ships as a set of Docker images. The recommended way to run it is with the official docker-compose.yml from the zenstats-deploy repository.

quickStart.heading: Quick Start
quickStart.step2: Copy and edit the environment file

envVars.heading: Key Environment Variables
envVars.secretKey: JWT signing secret. Required in production. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32
envVars.domain: Public hostname of your ZenStats instance (e.g. stats.example.com). Used in the tracking script snippet.
envVars.dbPassword: PostgreSQL password. Change from the default before deploying.
envVars.maxmindKey: MaxMind GeoLite2 license key for GeoIP resolution. Leave empty to use the Loyalsoldier fallback database.
envVars.logLevel: Log verbosity. One of: debug, info, warn, error. Default: info.

services.heading: Services
services.frontend: Caddy-based reverse proxy serving the React frontend and proxying API calls. Handles TLS automatically.
services.backend: Go API server. Handles event ingestion, authentication, and analytics queries.
services.postgres: PostgreSQL — stores users, sites, goals, funnels, and configuration.
services.clickhouse: ClickHouse — stores raw pageview and event data for analytics queries.

deployment.callout: Data is persisted in named Docker volumes (db-data, event-data, zenstats-data). Back these up regularly.

shields.description: Traffic shields let you filter out unwanted traffic before it reaches your analytics. Configure them in Site Settings → Shields.

ip.heading: IP Blacklist
ip.description: Block incoming events from specific IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. Useful for excluding your own office IP or known bots.

hostname.heading: Hostname Allowlist
hostname.description: Only accept events where the request hostname matches an allowed entry. Wildcards are supported at the start (e.g. *.example.com). Leave the list empty to allow all hostnames.

country.heading: Country Blacklist
country.description: Block all traffic from specific countries using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g. CN, RU). Requires GeoIP to be configured.

referrer.heading: Spam Referrer Blacklist
referrer.description: Block events whose Referer header matches a known spam domain. Add domains one at a time.

shields.callout: Shield rules are evaluated on every inbound event before it is written to ClickHouse. Blocked events are dropped silently and do not appear in your analytics.

emailReports.description: ZenStats can send automated summary reports to site owners. Reports compare the current period against the previous one and include top pages, sources, and key metrics.

weekly.heading: Weekly Report
weekly.description: Sent every Monday at 8:00 AM (server timezone). Covers the previous full week.

monthly.heading: Monthly Report
monthly.description: Sent on the 1st of each month at 9:00 AM (server timezone). Covers the previous full month.

emailReports.callout: Email reports require SMTP to be configured in Admin → Settings. Toggle them on per site in Site Settings → Email Reports.

trafficAlerts.description: Traffic alerts notify you by email when your site traffic changes significantly compared to the same time last week.

settings.heading: Configuration
settings.threshold: Percentage change required to trigger an alert. For example, a threshold of 30 fires when traffic increases or decreases by more than 30%.
settings.interval: Comparison granularity: hourly (last hour vs. same hour last week) or daily (today vs. same day last week).
settings.recipients: Comma-separated list of additional email recipients. The site owner is always notified.

trafficAlerts.callout: Traffic alerts require SMTP to be configured in Admin → Settings. Enable them per site in Site Settings → Traffic Alerts.

subAccounts.description: Sub-accounts are additional login users under a parent account. Each sub-account has a role and a set of fine-grained write permissions; it can always view analytics for sites it is a member of, but can only modify what its permissions allow.

roles.heading: Roles
roles.editor: Can manage goals, funnels, segments, and shared links.
roles.custom: Any custom combination of the write permissions below.

permissions.heading: Write permissions
permissions.description: A sub-account may hold any subset of these. Without a permission, the corresponding write API returns 403; reads are unaffected. Site creation/deletion, API keys, and sub-account management remain parent-account only.
permissions.sharedLinks: Create and delete shared dashboard links.
permissions.shields: Manage IP / hostname / country / referrer shield rules.
permissions.trafficAlerts: Configure traffic alert thresholds and recipients.

subAccounts.callout: Permission and status changes take effect on the sub-account's next token refresh; a suspended sub-account is signed out automatically.

metrics.bounceRate: Percentage of sessions with a single pageview.
metrics.timeOnPage: Average time spent on a page before navigating away.
metrics.scrollDepth: Average percentage of the page scrolled.
metrics.exitRate: Percentage of sessions that ended on this page. Only supported with an event:page breakdown.
metrics.conversions: Unique visitors who completed a goal (requires goal filter).
metrics.conversionRate: Percentage of visitors who completed a goal (requires goal filter. Aggregate only).
metrics.percentage: Each group's share of total visitors, as a percentage. Breakdown queries only.
metrics.totalRevenue: Sum of event revenue (ecommerce). Requires events sent with a revenue amount.

dimensions.channel: Acquisition channel (Organic Search, Paid Search, Social, Referral, Direct, …).

filters.is: Exact match. Accepts multiple values (OR logic within one filter).
filters.matchesWildcard: Wildcard match (* matches any sequence). e.g. /blog/**
filters.hasDone: Sessions in which the given event filter occurred at least once.
filters.hasNotDone: Sessions in which the given event filter never occurred.

periods.custom: Custom date range. Use date_range in the v2 API.
periods.all: All available data (approximated to the last 5 years).
periods.shorthand: Relative shorthand: Nd = last N days, Nmo = last N months (e.g. 7d, 28d, 3mo).

heatmap.title: Click heatmap
heatmap.description: Explore captured clicks for each page layout. Heatmaps are separate from traffic analytics and do not add pageviews, visitors or business events.
heatmap.rulesHelp: Exact paths or a single-segment * wildcard, e.g. /pricing or /blog/*. * never crosses /. Omit query parameters; use /#/pricing for hash routes.
heatmap.timezone: Heatmap timezone: {{timezone}}. Fixed on first save so a later site timezone change cannot shift historical hour buckets.
heatmap.retentionHelp: Retention changes apply to new clicks. Defaults: 7 days raw, 90 days aggregate. Disabling takes about 10–30 seconds. The queue uses memory; 202 means queued. Administrators can inspect collection quality for write results.
heatmap.installHelp: Add data-heatmap="true" and a release version to your existing Tracker tag. Update the version with every layout release. Keep script.hash.js for hash routes. Both site settings and the script option must be enabled.
heatmap.privacyHelp: No text, form values, IP, UA or visitor identifiers are collected. data-zs-ignore excludes clicks. Use template names for aggregation keys, never user IDs or personal data.
heatmap.dateHelp: Calendar days in {{timezone}}. Counts reflect captured clicks and are not scaled up by the sampling rate.
heatmap.empty: No clicks in this period. Check the enabled site configuration, matching page rules, and the heatmap option on your Tracker script.
heatmap.pageLayout: Page / version / viewport → document size (CSS pixels)
heatmap.pageLimit: Showing the 200 most recently active layouts. Narrow the date range to see others.
heatmap.unknownVersion: This page has no release version. Historical screenshots may show a different layout. Set data-heatmap-version and verify the background.
heatmap.deleteConfirm: Delete this screenshot? Click data will be retained.
heatmap.snapshotHelp: Required: version {{version}}, viewport {{width}}×{{height}}, full document {{docWidth}}×{{docHeight}} CSS pixels. Capture the full page at that viewport. Proportional DPR scaling is supported. PNG/JPEG, ≤5 MiB, ≤25 megapixels. Redact personal information before uploading.
heatmap.noSnapshot: No matching background. Capture one automatically or upload a historical screenshot in URL mode.
heatmap.sampledCounts: Deduplicated by click ID. These are sampled clicks, not estimated total clicks or unique visitors.
heatmap.unmapped: Not projected: {{count}} (fixed, sticky, nested scrolling or zoom)
heatmap.truncated: More than 10,000 heat points: showing the hottest cells. The total includes all cells.
heatmap.elementsHelp: Only elements with data-zs-id labels. Top 100, including unprojected clicks.
heatmap.imageLimit: The screenshot must be at most 5 MiB.
heatmap.qualityScope: Counters for this instance since startup (reset on restart). Received and persisted counts include retries; queries deduplicate click IDs. A failed write may have partially committed. 202 only means queued in memory.
heatmap.groupsHelp: First matching rule overrides data-heatmap-key. Only identical hostname, version, variant, viewport and document dimensions are combined. Rules do not expand the collection allowlist or backfill historical data.
heatmap.groupLayoutHelp: Combine URLs sharing a key and identical layout dimensions. Different heights or viewports remain separate. Use the same template and update the version when content positions change.
heatmap.captureHelp: Captures the public page at the selected viewport without login cookies. Version, variant and document dimensions must match. Upload historical images in URL mode when necessary. Do not include query values or personal data.
heatmap.captureUnavailable: Screenshot service is not configured. Deploy the separate worker and set ZENSTATS_HEATMAP_SCREENSHOT_URL and ZENSTATS_HEATMAP_SCREENSHOT_TOKEN. Manual upload remains available in URL mode.
heatmap.captureReady: Screenshot service is configured. Generate backgrounds from the heatmap viewer.
heatmap.docOverview: Heatmaps are off by default. Site settings → Heatmap settings opens the list. Choose New heatmap to configure one path rule or aggregation key, or select an entry to inspect and edit its details. Sampling, retention and the collection switch are managed separately in Collection settings. Add data-heatmap="true" to the Tracker. Normal traffic collection is independent.
heatmap.docGroups: Map /soft/*.html to software-detail and provide an example URL to view similar pages by key. A script can also set data-heatmap-key. The first matching path rule takes precedence. Original URLs remain available and new rules only affect future clicks.
heatmap.docLayout: Key views still separate hostname, version, variant, viewport and document dimensions. Equal dimensions do not guarantee equal layouts: only combine the same template and update data-heatmap-version when positions change. Different heights are never stretched together. Fixed, sticky and nested-scroll elements count but are not projected onto a full-page image.
heatmap.docScreenshot: Select dates and a layout, enter the specific URL or rule example URL, and capture a background. A separate browser generates a full-page PNG at that viewport. Version and dimensions are verified before saving. Public HTTP(S) pages only, with no login state. Private destinations are blocked by default. Manual upload is available without a worker.
heatmap.docRetention: Raw clicks default to 7 days and hourly aggregates to 90 days, configurable per site. Dates use the frozen site timezone. Counts reflect actual sampled clicks without extrapolation; repeated click IDs are deduplicated. HTTP 202 means in-memory acceptance only. Administrators can inspect collection quality.
heatmap.docAPI: Query and snapshot APIs use JWT and site membership. Members can read; parent-account site owners/admins can configure, capture, upload and delete. The screenshot worker is internal only; never expose its token to the Tracker or frontend.
heatmap.configuredHelp: Select a name or Details to inspect one heatmap, or choose New heatmap to create one. Configurations appear even before any clicks are collected.
heatmap.noConfigured: No heatmaps yet. Choose New heatmap to configure one.
heatmap.removeConfiguredConfirm: Delete the heatmap configuration for "{{name}}"? Collected data and backgrounds keep their retention periods. Shared allowed paths may still permit collection. Removing the last allowed path turns off heatmap collection for the site.
heatmap.configurationNotFound: This configuration no longer exists or has changed. Return to the list and select it again.
heatmap.invalidRulePath: Enter a path starting with /. A single-segment * is supported; query values and other wildcards are not.
heatmap.invalidGroupKey: Enter a valid aggregation key (1–120 letters, digits or _. : / @ - characters).
heatmap.duplicatePath: A heatmap already uses this path. Edit the existing configuration from the list.
heatmap.entryCollectionHelp: Saving adds this path to the collection allowlist. Sampling, retention and the collection switch are managed in the site Collection settings. The Tracker must still opt in to data-heatmap. Changing a path or key affects future collection only; historical data keeps its original dimensions.
heatmap.sharedCollectionHelp: Shared site settings: {{sample}}% sampling, raw clicks retained for {{raw}} days, aggregates for {{aggregate}} days
heatmap.collectionScopeHelp: These settings apply to every heatmap on this site. Select an individual heatmap in the list to edit its path, aggregation key or example URL.
